text:
nina (People Ops): Heads-up: made a tiny peer-feedback + calibration kit for managers prepping for the Q-cycle. 1-page copy/paste snippets, a short peer-feedback script, and a calibration 90s checklist. Drop in 1:1s or panel notes. Link: https://intranet.redwood/people-ops/mini-kits

mike (Eng Manager): super useful. can you share the one-liner peers can use when asked for feedback publicly? i want it friendly and non-judgmental.

nina (People Ops): PUBLIC PEER-REPLY (1-liner)
- "Thanks for asking! I9ll DM a couple quick notes to be specific; if you want public kudos, say 'share' and I9ll post a short highlight here.

rana (Design): love that. any short scripts for managers to moderate self-reviews that are vague?

nina (People Ops): MODERATOR PROMPT (for vague self-reviews)
- "Thanks for this summary. Can you add 1-2 measurable outcomes (metrics, number of users impacted, time saved) and one concrete example of a decision you led? That helps calibration and coachable next steps."

mike (Eng Manager): ok. what about a short peer-feedback template for panels to paste in slack threads?

nina (People Ops): PEER FEEDBACK TEMPLATE (3 lines)
1) "Strength: [name] consistently [what they do well]."
2) "Example: On [project], they [specific action and outcome]."
3) "Suggestion: Next, consider [one concrete growth action]."

oscar (HireOps): can we add an interview feedback micro-template for hiring panels? keeps forms tight.

nina (People Ops): INTERVIEW MICRO-TEMPLATES
- HIRE: "Clear system thinking, strong ownership examples, recommend hire for [level]."
- BORDERLINE: "Strong technical foundations; follow-up loop on product tradeoffs or cross-team influence recommended."
- NO-HIRE: "Gaps in [area], needs more experience in [skill]; not recommended."

nina (People Ops): CALIBRATION 90s CHECKLIST (use during panels or quick calibration calls)
- "1) Impact: name one measurable result this person influenced; 2) Reliability: did they meet key commitments? (yes/some/no); 3) Growth signal: did they mentor or expand scope? (yes/no). Quick mapping: high=impact+reliable+growth, med=team-impact+mostly reliable, low=limited impact or recurring misses."

mike (Eng Manager): quick ask: any short timeline phrasing managers can paste when setting an improvement plan?

nina (People Ops): TIMELINE SNIPPET
- "We9ll try this approach for the next 6 weeks with a 2-week check-in. If we see steady progress we9ll continue; if not we9ll adjust the plan."

rana (Design): can you include one compact OKR example for cross-functional work? something we can copy into product or design goals.

nina (People Ops): CROSS-FUNC OKR (compact)
- "Objective: Speed up cross-team launches. KR1: Reduce average cross-team launch time from 10w to 6w. KR2: Create 3 shared kickoff templates and run 2 joint rehearsals. KR3: Increase post-launch satisfaction score from 72 to 85."

review-bot: Reminder: Q-cycle self-reviews open in 9 days. Use /start-review to begin.

nina (People Ops): If you want a Google Doc with level-specific phrasing (IC2/IC3/Senior/Staff), react :doc: and we9ll prioritize staff-level examples first. Thanks!

mike (Eng Manager): thanks nina, this is going straight into my 1:1 notes.
